correctness.rationale: Exact leaf-splitting root decomposition and independence give the displayed covariance recursion with conditional forcing \(4(1-H_{n-2})/[3(n-1)]\); evaluating the sum cancels harmonic terms and proves the finite identity by induction. \(n=2,3\) boundary behavior is explicit, and variance recurrence proves the cherry slope for \(n\ge5\). Correlation combines this with the independently checked, already established Sackin variance of Cardona et al. A standalone verifier passed 754 exact-rational assertions, exhaustive independent leaf-splitting histories through nine leaves and moment recurrences through 120; experiments are not an infinite proof. No unstated normal approximation is assumed.

originality.rationale: The final exact closed finite-size cherry–Sackin covariance, strict negative sign, linear regression coefficient and asymptotic Pearson coefficient are not stated by the inspected primary literature. Choi–Thompson–Wu characterize cherry/pitchforks; Cardona–Mir–Rosselló treat Sackin variance and Sackin–cophenetic covariance, with C denoting Colless and not cherry count. Their generic second-moment recurrence is an applicable method but does not directly evaluate this new cross-moment. Janzen–Etienne report model-dependent metric correlations numerically. Deduplication compared exact statements/implications and the distribution, not merely title wording. A historical implicit derivation remains a nonzero risk.
residual_risks: The broad 2012 recursive-shape-index theory might have been specialized to this exact Yule cherry–Sackin moment in an uncatalogued older article, book, appendix, or thesis. An exhaustive historical priority guarantee is not possible from the inspected evidence.

value.rationale: Cherries measure local two-tip clades; the Sackin sum measures global root-to-leaf imbalance. Literature reports model-dependent correlation clustering without furnishing this exact pairwise Yule benchmark. The result gives all finite sizes, a universal negative sign, linear-scale covariance, a sharp optimal linear prediction slope, and the explicit decay of Pearson correlation, enabling principled joint-statistic calibration. These are naturally motivated interpretable quantities, not arbitrary parameter slices or a mere recomputation of known individual moments.
